hadith:
The Two Festivals (Eids) - Narrated `Abdur Rahman bin `Abis:

Ibn `Abbas was asked whether he had joined the Prophet (ﷺ) in the `Id prayer. He said, "Yes. And I could not have joined him had I not been young. (The Prophet (ﷺ) came out) till he reached the mark which was near the house of Kathir bin As-Salt, offered the prayer, delivered the Khutba and then went towards the women. Bilal was accompanying him. He preached to them and advised them and ordered them to give alms. I saw the women putting their ornaments with their outstretched hands into Bilal's garment. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) along with Bilal returned home.
message: Moses asked Allah for support in his task, and Allah granted his request—a reminder to seek His help in doing good. Remembering Allah as Al-Kabeer, the Greatest, can inspire humility and generosity, as the Prophet ﷺ encouraged women to give charity on Eid.
name:
Al Kabeer - الْكَبِيرُ - The Greatest

The term Al Kabeer highlights Allah's unparalleled magnitude, authority, and grandeur, reminding believers of His infinite power and majesty. The name originates from the Arabic root 'K-B-R,' meaning 'to be great or to be large.' It is found in various Islamic texts, emphasizing the significance of recognizing Allah's greatness in worship and daily life.
